license_note: Dimensional facts about commercial launch rails, launch rods, rail buttons and launch lugs. Extrusion profiles are 80/20 Inc. (10-series '1010', 15-series '1515') and Unistrut (P1000) catalog dimensions and generic metric T-slot profiles; rail-button dimensions are Rail-Buttons.com, Binder Design and Wildman Rocketry product dimensions as republished in OpenRocket's RailButton_Database.orc (GPL-licensed data file; the numbers themselves are facts); lug dimensions are Estes and LOC Precision product dimensions as republished in OpenRocket's legacy component files. Screw dimensions are ASME B1.1 and ASME B18.2.8. Numbers are facts, not copyrightable; cite the vendor / standard. Vendor web sites and the 80/20 and Unistrut drawings were NOT reachable during compilation; every value not marked certain or likely is recall and must be verified on the physical rail before cutting metal.

columns.key: unique row id (stable; CAD tool references these)
columns.item: human name of the rail / rod / button / lug
columns.vendor: manufacturer the dimensions are attributed to (null for generic / standard-defined rows)
columns.part_number: vendor part number as the source document gives it (null if none)
columns.fits: buttons: key of the rail row this button mates with; lugs: key of the rod row; rails/rods: null
columns.extrusion_size_in: rail only: nominal square extrusion size, inches (exact as the vendor states it; for metric rails this is the 3 dp conversion and the mm value is primary)
columns.extrusion_size_mm: rail only: same, millimetres (3 dp; primary for metric rails)
columns.slot_opening_in: rail only: width of the T-slot opening at the rail surface, inches. Button NECK DIAMETER must be LESS than this.
columns.slot_pocket_width_in: rail only: width of the T-slot pocket behind the lip, inches. Button HEAD DIAMETER must be LESS than this and MORE than slot_opening.
columns.slot_lip_thickness_in: rail only: material thickness of the lip between rail surface and pocket, inches. For a rolled channel (Unistrut) this is the SHEET GAUGE and is NOT the dimension a neck must span - use lip_engagement_depth for that.
columns.lip_engagement_depth_in: rail only: axial distance from the rail surface to the underside of the lip that the button head bears on, inches. Button NECK LENGTH must EXCEED this by 0.02-0.04 in clearance. Equals slot_lip_thickness for extruded T-slot; equals the inturned-lip RETURN depth for Unistrut-type channel.
columns.slot_depth_in: rail only: total depth from rail surface to bottom of pocket, inches (informational; see pocket_depth for the head-thickness check)
columns.pocket_depth_in: rail only: DERIVED = slot_depth - lip_engagement_depth, inches. Button HEAD THICKNESS must be LESS than this minus clearance. (Replaces the wrong 'head thickness + neck length < slot depth' rule of the compiled table.)
columns.head_dia_in: button only: diameter of the flange that rides INSIDE the T-slot pocket, inches (OpenRocket 'OuterDiameter'; vendors call this the button diameter; on every vendor button tabulated here head and base flange have the SAME diameter)
columns.head_thickness_in: button only: thickness of the in-slot head flange, inches (OpenRocket 'FlangeHeight')
columns.neck_dia_in: button only: diameter of the shank that passes through the slot opening, inches (OpenRocket 'InnerDiameter')
columns.neck_length_in: button only: axial length of the neck between head and base flange, inches. DERIVED = overall_height - head_thickness - base_flange_thickness
columns.base_flange_dia_in: button only: diameter of the outer flange that sits against the airframe, inches (same as head_dia on all tabulated vendor buttons)
columns.base_flange_thickness_in: button only: thickness of the base flange / standoff, inches (OpenRocket 'BaseHeight'). Needed for screw-length calculation.
columns.overall_height_in: button only: total height base-face to head-face, inches (OpenRocket 'Height'); the mounted standoff of the head face above the airframe surface
columns.screw_head_protrusion_in: button only: how far the supplied screw head stands above the head face, inches (OpenRocket 'ScrewHeight'; 0 = countersunk flush)
columns.screw_thread: button only: thread the vendor supplies the button for (UNC/UNF designation). A single value, not a list; substitutions are discussed in notes.
columns.screw_major_dia_in: button only: basic major diameter of screw_thread, inches (ASME B1.1)
columns.screw_clearance_hole_in: button only: 'normal' fit clearance hole for screw_thread per ASME B18.2.8, inches - the through-hole to drill in a MACHINED button or nut plate; vendor buttons come pre-drilled/countersunk
columns.mass_g: button only: mass of the button alone (no screw / nut), grams
columns.rod_dia_in: rod only: nominal launch-rod diameter, inches (exact fraction)
columns.lug_id_in: lug only: inside diameter of the commercial launch lug, inches
columns.lug_od_in: lug only: outside diameter of the commercial launch lug (paper/plastic tube), inches
columns.lug_length_in: lug only: length of the commercial lug as sold, inches
columns.confidence: row-level: certain | likely | recall - the LOWEST confidence of any numeric field in the row
columns.field_confidence: per-field confidence where it differs from the row level, {field: certain|likely|recall}
columns.disputed: alternatives offered by reviewers or other sources that were NOT adopted, as {field: 'value (who/source)'}; null if none
columns.source: standard or vendor document the values come from

notes: READ BEFORE CUTTING. (1) CONFIDENCE. Rod diameters and extrusion nominal sizes are exact by definition (certain). The 1010 slot opening 0.256 in and 1515 slot opening 0.320 in are widely republished and each is consistent with every vendor button neck in this table (likely). The six vendor rail-button rows are copied verbatim from OpenRocket's shipped RailButton_Database.orc, which attributes them to Rail-Buttons.com, Binder Design and Wildman (likely = vendor-attributed community data, not the vendor drawing; the same file contains at least two entries that are physically inconsistent, see (9), so caliper a real button before copying it in metal). Everything else - 80/20 pocket widths, lip thicknesses, slot depths, the Unistrut lip return, the metric 2020/3030 profiles, and all commercial lug ID/ODs - is recall or drawing-library approximation and MUST be measured on the actual rail or lug before machining. Per-field confidence is in field_confidence; row-level confidence is the lowest field. (2) FIT RULES (these replace the compiled table's wrong 'head thickness + neck length < slot depth' rule, which the compiled table itself violated). The neck spans the lip and stands OUTSIDE the rail surface; only the head sits in the pocket. Therefore: (a) neck_dia < slot_opening by 0.010-0.025 in total so a slightly twisted rail does not bind (design 0.230-0.245 in for 1010, 0.290-0.305 in for 1515, < 5.8 mm for 2020, < 7.8 mm for 3030); (b) slot_opening + 0.08 in < head_dia < slot_pocket_width - 0.08 in so the head cannot pull through the opening and cannot wedge in the pocket; (c) neck_length > lip_engagement_depth + 0.02-0.04 in so the button slides on the lip rather than clamping it (for Unistrut the engagement depth is the ~0.38 in inturned RETURN, not the 0.105 in sheet); (d) head_thickness < pocket_depth - 0.03 in; (e) screw clearance hole < neck_dia - 0.06 in (0.03 in wall each side minimum in Delrin; more in aluminium is not needed but a 1/4-20 hole in a 0.29 in 1515 neck is impossible - use a bigger button or a bigger rail, not a bigger screw in this button). (3) DESIGN ENVELOPE FOR A MACHINED RAIL GUIDE (Delrin/acetal/UHMW; derived from the rail rows and the vendor-button spread, so no better than the rail recall): 1010 - neck dia 0.235-0.245, neck length 0.145-0.160, head dia 0.36-0.44, head thickness 0.07-0.10, base flange dia = head dia (0.36-0.44), base thickness 0.07-0.10, total height 0.29-0.33 in, screw 8-32. 1515 - neck dia 0.290-0.305, neck length 0.180-0.200, head dia 0.49-0.62, head thickness 0.12-0.19, base dia = head dia, base thickness 0.12-0.34 (Wildman-style tall base 0.338 if extra standoff is wanted), total height 0.45-0.69 in, screw 10-32. Standoff (overall_height) differs by up to 0.24 in between vendors' 1515 buttons - both buttons on one rocket must be the SAME part number or a machined standoff must make up the difference. (4) MATERIAL. Do not machine a whole button from bare 6061: aluminium sliding in an anodised 80/20 slot galls and binds and can gouge the pad's rail. Make the in-slot head and neck from acetal (Delrin), UHMW or nylon; an aluminium base/standoff under a plastic head is fine. Delrin machines to +/-0.002 in easily, so do not chase tighter tolerances than the rail's own recall accuracy. (5) TWO BUTTONS, ONE LINE. Two buttons minimum, both on the same line parallel to the rocket axis, forward button near the CG and aft button as far aft as practical; both head faces must sit at the SAME radial distance from the rocket axis. If the aft button sits on a fin can, motor-retainer flange, coupler band, tailcone or a fin-root fillet where the local OD differs from the airframe OD under the forward button, add a machined standoff under the smaller-OD button: standoff height = (D_airframe - D_local)/2 (subtract any conformal-layer thickness the other button sits on), with the base face cut to the local radius so it beds, and increase that screw's length by the same amount. A standoff taller than about 0.5 in in plastic wants an aluminium body. (6) SCREW LENGTH AND BACKING. Screw length = button overall_height + airframe wall + conformal layers (fiberglass wrap, tip-to-tip layup, skin, standoff) + thread engagement in the backing. Minimum engagement (recall, rule of thumb): 1.0 x nominal diameter in aluminium or steel nut plate, i.e. 0.164 in for 8-32, 0.19 in for 10-32, 0.25 in for 1/4-20; in G10 or plywood do not thread the material - use a T-nut, nut plate, blind rivet nut or through-bolt to a centering ring, with the backing at least 0.125 in thick for #8, 0.19 in for #10 and 0.25 in for 1/4 (recall). Never rely on threads in the airframe wall alone above mid-power. Screw major diameters used here are ASME B1.1: #4 0.112, #6 0.138, #8 0.164, #10 0.190, 1/4 0.250 in (certain). Normal-fit clearance holes are ASME B18.2.8: #6 0.1495, #8 0.1770, #10 0.2010, 1/4 0.2660 in (likely); M4 (4.000 mm, ISO 261) with a 4.5 mm hole (ISO 273 medium) is an acceptable substitute for #8 and M5 (5.5 mm hole) for #10. (7) SCREW HEAD IN A MACHINED BUTTON. Vendor buttons use countersunk (82 deg flat head) screws flush with the head face. If you machine your own, a socket-head counterbore needs head_dia - counterbore >= 0.06 in wall each side: SHCS head diameters (recall, ASME B18.3) #6 0.226, #8 0.270, #10 0.312, 1/4 0.375 in - so an SHCS fits a 0.44-0.62 in head but NOT the 0.3725 in 1P1010DLX geometry; use a flat head there. A screw head must not protrude above the head face (screw_head_protrusion = 0) unless pocket_depth allows it. (8) RAILS AT THE PAD. '1010' and '1515' are 80/20 PART NUMBERS (10-series 1.00 in, 15-series 1.50 in), not slot sizes. 80/20-compatible extrusions from Misumi, TSLOTS, Faztek and generic imports, and the many 2020/3030 clones and V-slot profiles, have slot openings and lip geometry that differ by up to 0.01-0.02 in / 0.2-0.5 mm from these rows. The pad's rail is the standard; caliper its opening, lip and pocket before finalising a machined guide, and always test-slide the finished part on the rail before flight. Unistrut/Superstrut/B-Line channel comes in 12 ga (0.105) and 14 ga (0.075) and in slotted and solid-back forms; only the 12 ga P1000 envelope is tabulated. Rule of thumb for rail choice (recall, not a standard): 1010 up to roughly 20-30 lb liftoff mass, 1515 above that, Unistrut for very large research vehicles. (9) ROWS DROPPED AND ITEMS NOT ADDED. Dropped button_1010_mini: the compiled numbers were invented from the slot envelope and the only open-source record (Rail-Buttons.com 1PMB in the ORC file: OD 0.249, neck 0.193, height 0.205, flanges 0.038, 0.090 g) has a head SMALLER than the 1010 slot opening 0.256, so it cannot be retained by a 1010 rail as recorded - do not cut a mini until a real one is measured. Dropped button_unistrut: the compiled row (head 1.2, head thk 0.4, neck 0.8 x 0.45, base 1.25, height 1.0 in, 1/4-20) was derived, not recalled or sourced; the fitness skeptic judged it too uncertain to cut, and a 0.80 in neck in a 0.875 in rolled opening leaves 0.075 in total clearance. Design one from the rail_unistrut_1625 envelope using rule (2) after measuring the channel. Not added - Rail-Buttons.com RB-Micro (10 mm rail, 2-56): the ORC entry lists FlangeHeight 0 and there is no 10 mm rail row; Rail-Buttons.com RB-10-D 3-piece 1010 (OD 0.278, neck 0.154, height 0.270): its 0.154 in neck is SMALLER than the 8-32 screw it is listed with (0.164 major) and its head overlaps the 1010 lip by only 0.011 in per side, so the entry is internally inconsistent. All three are evidence that the ORC database is community data with errors; the six buttons that were adopted pass every fit rule in (2) against the rail rows. (10) LUGS AND RODS. Rod diameter (certain) is the only number to cut to: machine a lug ID = rod + 0.030-0.050 in (9/32 in drill for a 1/4 in rod), lug length >= 2-3 x rod diameter per lug to stop cocking, two lugs on one line parallel to the axis. Commercial lug ID/OD rows are informational (recall/likely) for modelling mass and drag, not for machining. Rods are often 0.003-0.005 in under nominal and can be bent - do not size to a measured rod. (11) ROUNDING. mm = in x 25.4 rounded half-up to 3 dp (so 0.1875 in -> 4.763, not 4.762 under banker's rounding). For the metric rails the mm value is primary and the inch column is the 3 dp conversion. Three-decimal mm values on a 'recall' row imply nothing about accuracy; treat recall rail internals as +/-0.5 mm until measured. COUNTS: rows changed 8 (rail_1010, rail_1515, rail_unistrut_1625, button_1010_std, button_1515_std, lug_rod_0125, lug_rod_01875, lug_rod_025), rows dropped 2 (button_1010_mini, button_unistrut), rows added 10 (rail_2020, rail_3030, rod_0125, rod_01875, rod_025, rod_05, button_1010_binder, button_1515_binder, button_1515_wildman, lug_rod_05); 10 compiled rows -> 18 final rows.

verified_directly: OpenRocket RailButton_Database.orc and RailButton.java fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com; flange/base/neck semantics confirmed from the source comment block (OuterDiameter is the single OD of both flanges).
OpenRocket Estes-legacy.orc and LocPrecision-legacy.orc launch-lug entries fetched and converted from metres.

reconciliation.rule_application: Where the spot-check skeptic supplied vendor values from the ORC file, the compiled values (which the compiled source strings admitted were 'inferred from the slot envelope') had no stronger source and were replaced. The rule 'confidence = lower of the two' would give 'recall'; because the cited file was fetched and read directly it is a document value, labelled 'likely' with the file's known defects stated in notes (9). Where a skeptic only offered a recall alternative without a document (80/20 pocket/lip/depth, Unistrut return depth) the compiled value was kept at 'recall' with a 'disputed' field. Rows the fitness skeptic said were too uncertain to cut from were dropped and recorded in notes (9).
structural_changes: slot_depth column rule ('head thickness + neck length < slot depth') was wrong and self-violated; replaced by pocket_depth (derived) and lip_engagement_depth fields with the geometric rules in notes (2).
Unistrut: 0.105 in sheet gauge kept as slot_lip_thickness; the ~0.38 in inturned-lip return moved out of prose into lip_engagement_depth_in/mm (recall).

Buttons: head and base now carry the vendor's single OD; base_flange_thickness, screw_head_protrusion, mass_g, screw_thread (single value), screw_major_dia (ASME B1.1) and screw_clearance_hole (ASME B18.2.8) added; free-text mounting_screw column removed; the '1/4-20 for heavy rockets' remark on the 1515 button struck (0.012 in neck wall).
Lugs now 'fit' a rod row key; four 'rod' rows added carrying the certain rod diameters separately from the recall lug tubes; lug_length added.
Per-field confidence added (field_confidence) and a 'disputed' field for non-adopted alternatives; row-level confidence is the lowest field.
vendor and part_number columns added so a row can be matched to a listing.
missing_items_not_supplied: Rail-Buttons.com RB-Micro and RB-10-D and 1PMB (ORC entries internally inconsistent; see notes 9).
Apogee-branded button dimensions (no document reachable; Apogee resells Rail-Buttons.com parts by recall).
80/20 pocket / lip / depth from the actual drawing (still recall).
